headline: Bitcoin Tops $60,000 as Risk Assets Rise in Holiday Trading
author: Emily Nicolle

paragraphs.text: Thu, November 26, 2026 at 8:28 AM PST 2 min read
(Bloomberg) -- Bitcoin rose above the $60,000 mark on Thursday as risky assets tracked a rebound in tech equities, pushing crypto markets higher as they head into a period of thin holiday trading.

The largest cryptocurrency rose as much as 2.2% during the Asia session before paring some of those gains, changing hands at around $60,500 in New York trading. Other tokens including Ether and XRP also rose.

Bitcoin has lost more than a fifth of its value this month, putting it on course for its biggest monthly decline since a crypto-market meltdown more than four years ago. The sector has struggled to regain investor confidence amid a string of high-profile hacks, rising macroeconomic pressure and regulatory uncertainty following the US midterm elections.
"The rebound has improved the tape," analysts at Marex wrote in a note Thursday. "It has not repaired the underlying demand picture."

A set of US exchange-traded funds tracking the price of Bitcoin recorded $453 million in outflows on Wednesday, taking the group's outflows over the past month above $5 billion. The products launched to great fanfare in January 2024, but performance has faltered under dampened demand for the underlying asset.

"With ETF selling still running at a heavy pace, Bitcoin may have found some short-term breathing room, but there is a real risk that the sellers return once the holiday dust settles, leaving the recent lows back in sight," said Axel Rudolph, chief technical analyst at IG.
